title: Hosting a reading
hookLine: families host an akhand path or sehaj path for thanks or remembrance
tomorrow: Vaisakhi is coming. can a house in mourning celebrate?

lines: A READING IN THE FRONT ROOM.
cards: A few weeks on, Bebe's chilies are turning red, and she's made a list on the back of an envelope. Baba Kartar's birthday is next month. She wants a reading of the Guru Granth Sahib here, in the front room, for him.
Harjit reads the list over her shoulder and says, let's call it a thanks. For his long life. For Gurnam.
For all of it. Bebe frowns. Simran, setting the table, waits to see which word wins: remembrance, or thanks.

teach.b: Neither has to win. Sikh families host a reading at home for remembrance, for thanks, or both: an akhand path, read without a break from start to finish by readers taking turns, or a sehaj path, read at an unhurried pace.
The front room becomes a small gurdwara for a while: cleaned, a raised place for the Granth, a canopy, the sangat in and out, food for everyone.
Here's something to tell a friend tonight: a Sikh home can host the Guru for a whole reading, and grief and thanks can share the same one.
Now look back at the week that led here. The river: return to water. The sign-up sheet: read for them.
The rolling pin that kept going: grief is human. The locker room: in his will. The gurdwara kitchen: remember with seva.
Not so long ago, Baba Kartar was feeding sparrows at dawn. Bebe crosses out remembrance and writes both. Then, at the bottom of the list, in her slow handwriting: Simran reads first.

how: Sikh families host an akhand path or sehaj path at home or in a gurdwara to give thanks or to remember someone, with the Guru Granth Sahib installed with respect, kirtan, Ardas at the bhog, karah prashad and langar for the guests.

o: welcoming the Guru home for a full reading
reading a favorite book aloud to the family
throwing a birthday party with music and cake

games.q: two weeks, six lines — tap the pairs.

s: an akhand path is read without a break, start to finish
readers take turns so the reading never stops.
a home reading can be held only after a death
families host for thanks too, or for both at once.
you need a gurdwara building to host a reading
a front room can host the Guru, made ready with respect.

games.q: your family wants to host a reading for your grandfather's birthday, but your aunt says it's 'too sad' and your uncle says it's 'too soon to celebrate.' what fits?
o: cancel it; if people disagree, it isn't meant to be.
hold it for both: remembering him and giving thanks for him.
make it only a thanks, and don't mention him at all.
games.why: Bebe crossed out remembrance and wrote both. a reading can hold grief and thanks at the same time.

practice: Think of a reason your home could host something: a thanks, a remembrance, a new start. While the sit runs, make a small plan: who you'd invite, what would be read or sung, and the one thing most likely to get in the way.
You don't have to host anything; the plan is the practice.

wordCard.voice: Hosting a reading. Sikh families welcome the Guru Granth Sahib home for an akhand or sehaj path, in thanks or in remembrance.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: akhand path, an unbroken reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

carryVoice: Last line of these two weeks: host the word, for grief and for thanks at once. Baba would approve.

sources.ref: Sikh Rehat Maryada (akhand path and sehaj path; installing the Guru Granth Sahib with respect), paraphrased
